independence: Only the two specified new input files were read. No execution.json, validator implementation, prior assessment for this brief, other assessors' findings, network, database, provider or deployment was consulted. The assignment explicitly highlighted the page-layout ambiguity, so this was not a fully blinded assessment. The remaining assessment was independent.
deliveryStatus: There is no final validated pack. This assesses captured RAW copy only and does not establish delivery, validation or publication success.

rubric.scale: 0=unusable/absent; 1=weak; 2=adequate with substantial editing; 3=good with editing; 4=strong for the requested purpose.
rubric.interpretation: Editorial scores assess writing, audience/brand relevance and usable format structure. They do not override material factual findings. Metaphors, subjective permission and clearly hypothetical examples are not automatically factual failures.

criticalFactualVerdict.rootIssue: Unconfirmed physical page layout is repeatedly presented as a confirmed Fieldline specification.
criticalFactualVerdict.countingRule: Count one finding per materially unsupported asset assertion; the main video's spoken and on-screen versions are grouped into one finding. These are repetitions of one root issue, not ten independent inventions.
criticalFactualVerdict.keyConclusion: A5 paper format and three printed section headings do NOT establish three headings printed on every individual page. They also do not establish that a page is divided into three areas or that all three headings share one page.
criticalFactualVerdict.certainty: The brief is silent about page-by-page placement. The raw claims are unsupported, not proven physically false.

editorialTotals.summary: Mostly readable, gentle and coherent with the unfinished-page theme. Concrete imaginary-square details add interest. Product awareness is weaker in unbranded short assets; repeated page/permission language limits variety. The repurposed video has unfinished scaffolding. These editorial totals do not certify factual safety.

titleAndSummary.assessment: The pack title and summary name Fieldline, its three headings and the authorized unfinished-page creative stance. Neither specifies the headings' page-by-page placement or claims measured outcomes. They are internal pack metadata, not proof of successful delivery.

sourceQuotes: Its new notebook, Fieldline, has an A5 paper format and three printed section headings: Notice, Sketch, and Revisit.

sourceAudit.assessment: Names, A5 format, moss-green colour, the three heading names and intended informal-observation audience are supported. Per-page repetition, co-location and page divisions are not.

sourceQuotes: Current notebook information replaces the old saved brand offer of a waterproof travel journal.
sourceAudit.assessment: No waterproof or weather-resistant claim appears in the assets. References to imaginary outdoor places do not by themselves claim weather resistance.

The 28 minutes is only the event duration, not a promise of improved creativity, observation, productivity or wellbeing.
sourceAudit.assessment: The assets omit the event, Rowan and 28-minute duration. Consequently no duration-to-outcome conversion or invented event activity was found. The brief's central requested goal is notebook awareness, so omission of the separate event is not itself a factual failure.

sourceQuotes: Clearly hypothetical notes about an imaginary square are welcome as creative examples, not product features, event curriculum or customer experiences.
sourceAudit.assessment: The imaginary-square sounds, chalk, bench, fountain and map details are explicitly hypothetical where developed. They are not evidence of actual customers or promised event curriculum. A hypothetical note may use all three headings conceptually without proving their physical co-location.

sourceQuotes: Create engaging awareness content about the three headings and the freedom to leave a page unfinished.
sourceAudit.assessment: 'No pressure', 'calm', 'without guilt', 'still a complete page' and 'permission' are read as subjective creative framing. No measurable creativity, productivity, observation or wellbeing improvement is promised. These phrases should not later be repurposed as proven benefits.

sourceQuotes: No CTA anywhere, including captions, questions, scripts and hashtags: no requests to book, buy, visit, click, follow, save, share, comment, message or subscribe.
Leave CTA suggestion items empty with a short neutral explanation.
sourceAudit.assessment: All CTA fields are empty and the CTA set is empty. No listed commercial/social engagement request or audience-response question appears. 'Try one line' and the numbered Fill/Add/Leave steps are practice instructions rather than engagement solicitations. A literal ban on every directive would also reject them; safest editing is to frame them as optional hypothetical examples. This interpretation risk is not counted as a confirmed factual fabrication or definite engagement-CTA failure.

sourceQuotes: Avoid publisher-facing instructions.
sourceAudit.assessment: Script beat/on-screen labels, subject headers and carousel outline labels are appropriate formats. However, the nested video beat 'Optional imaginary square example for each heading' supplies a writing instruction rather than a finished example or spoken line.

coverage.scope: Title and summary; every section title, platform, body, item and CTA; all three Instagram and TikTok alternatives; twelve YouTube keyword items; six thread posts; full five-beat script and on-screen lines; eight carousel slides; three subject alternatives; seven nested repurposed assets including eight carousel slides and three video beats; eight hooks; six platform hashtag/keyword sets.
coverage.excluded: No execution evidence, final validated output, actual notebook/photos, actual video, external facts or other assessments.

1) Fill one line in Notice.
2) Add the smallest mark in Sketch.
3) Leave Revisit blank on purpose.
editorialIssues.issue: Useful illustrative practice, but its single-page arrangement follows the unverified physical layout. Frame it explicitly as an optional way to arrange notes. The imperatives are notebook-use guidance, not requests for commercial or social engagement.

editorialIssues.quote: That is still a complete page.
editorialIssues.issue: An acceptable creative definition of completeness, not a claim that the notebook performs a task. Similar language recurs throughout the pack.

formats.assessment: Product name, A5 format, cover colour and intended audience are faithful. The actual per-page printing claim is material. The body is readable but longer and more instructional than necessary for the requested concise awareness content.

editorialIssues.quote: Leaving the page unfinished is part of the method.

Clear and warm, with relatively concrete imagery; local framing should not imply an officially specified page layout.

priorityEdits: Remove every-page/each-page/per-page language from all eight explicit findings, including the full video's on-screen overlay.
Replace TikTok's single-page three-prompt description and the carousel's page-division claim with notebook-level confirmed facts, or request product-layout confirmation.
Keep clearly optional imaginary examples, but separate the suggested arrangement of notes from assertions about the product's printing.
Write the nested video's missing example as actual copy; reduce duplication and add Fieldline/Margin Tide to standalone awareness assets that currently omit both.
Use hypothetical phrasing instead of 'Try' or Fill/Add/Leave if the desired No CTA policy is literally directive-free.
